text.default:
You walk back along the east road to Crestfall.

There are three of you, you and [missing person] and Pol. Seriva and her soldiers went another way. They were not exactly avoiding you, but they were not walking with you either.

For the first time in fourteen months [missing person] is walking in ordinary daylight. They don't say so, and there is no need. You can see it in the way they look at the light coming through the ordinary trees, the trees with birds in them, and bark the proper colour.

default: Two miles back the deep forest begins, and it is still wrong in there. The seal stops the spread, but it doesn't undo fourteen months of change overnight. The Watcher is still at the gate, and the ruins are still ruins.

default.text: But the note you have carried in your bones since you came to Ashenveld is quieter. You can still find it if you listen.
default.else: But the note you have carried in your bones since you came to Ashenveld is quieter. It hasn't gone. It has changed, as a very loud noise changes when you walk away from it.

text.commander:
You walk, and go over it as you always do after anything big.

The job is done; the curse is sealed. Nobody was killed. Of the damage, to the afflicted people and the animals and the land, you know nothing yet, because the text said nothing clear about undoing it.

There is a good deal still to settle: where Vorne stands in Crestfall, what terms Seriva made, if any, and [missing person], who has been in the ruins fourteen months while the world outside forgot they existed.

You have a great deal of work ahead of you.
text.arcane:
You are thinking about the afflicted.

The seal stops the mechanism making any more of the curse. But the curse is already in Ashenveld, in the soil and the water and the stone and the people who have been near it. The seal does not take away what is already there. It only stops any more being added.

Whether what is there will fade, now that the source is sealed, you cannot say. The text called the sealing complete, which suggests that things go back to how they were. But how they were was kept so by a working mechanism in a living city, not by a sealed crack in an empty ruin.

You will have to watch carefully.
text.ranger:
The east road is not what it was. The deer that walked wrong have not come right in the few hours since the sealing, and you didn't expect them to. But as you walk you read the forest, and it tells you that something has changed at the source. Nothing new is coming from it. What is already in the land is still there, but it is not being fed any more.

When you shut a sluice the river does not run dry at once. But it does in the end.
text.cipher:
You think about what happens next. The practical questions you can manage.

The mechanism showed the two of you things about each other you would not have found out in ten more years of ordinary talk. The ruins did not tell you what to do with them.

choices.text: Talk to [missing person] as you walk, and begin to make sense of it.

default.text:
You talk as you walk, not about the ritual but about what happens now: where they go from here, and what Ashenveld will be now that the seal is made.

"I am not going back in," they say. "The chamber, the ruins. I have finished with it." They pause. "I am ready to have finished with it."

"Where do you want to go?" you ask.

They think about it for a long time. The road goes by under your feet, and the ordinary forest is all round you.

"I do not know yet," they say. "That may be the best thing that has happened to me in a year. Not knowing where I want to go."

choices.text: Walk without talking. Some things don't need words yet.

default.text:
You walk, and Pol walks, and [missing person] walks.

None of you says much. It is not that you have nothing to say. You have more than the road home could hold, and you have all decided to wait until you are somewhere quiet enough to say it properly.

At the Compact checkpoint the soldiers look hard at [missing person], as men do at a face that is not in their books. You give them a short account, and they let you through.

Crestfall is ahead of you.

default: The news goes round Crestfall as big news does in a small frightened town. First it is a rumour, and then people go about asking each other whether it is true, and then it is a fact that they hold on to cautiously, before they dare hold it tight.

Something has happened in the ruins. The one who went east has come back, and with them is somebody who has been in the ruins for more than a year. And the thing in the ground, which people have felt in the walls and the low places and the well water, is different today.

default.text:
Aldous is in the chair by the fire that used to be Wren's. He doesn't look up when the door opens.

It is Hanna, behind the bar, who sees you first. "They're back," she says, to nobody in particular. Then, louder, to the room: "They're back."
default.else:
Aldous is the first person you see when you come into the Tallow. He looks at [missing person] as you look at somebody you had given up for dead and have not yet got used to being wrong about.

"They're back," he says, not to you but to himself. Then, louder, to the room: "They're back."

text.commander:
The people in the Tallow have waited a long time for something to change, and now they are trying to decide whether this is the change they were waiting for.

You keep a hand on what gets said, and to whom, and in what order. The Compact ought to hear it from Vorne and not from gossip. And the Covenant will want careful handling.
text.arcane:
People ask you questions you can only half answer. Will the afflicted get better? How long will it take? Will the curse go out of the land? Will the people of Harrow come back?

You give them what answers you have, which are not complete, and you don't pretend to be surer than you are. You have found that it is the only way to keep people's trust at such times.
text.ranger:
You watch Crestfall take the news as you would watch any creatures take a change in their surroundings, keeping an eye out for the ones who take it oddly.

Wren isn't in the Tallow. He went east weeks ago. You don't know whether the seal will bring him back, or whether what the curse did to him can be undone.

The ritual answered that question in principle. It has not yet answered it in fact.
text.cipher:
What Crestfall knows is changing by the minute. You watch it, and take stock: what people know, what they think they know, what the Compact knows, and what Seriva will say when she gets back to town.

At the moment the story of what happened in the ruins is being told by whoever speaks first and loudest. You think about what the story ought to be, and who ought to tell it.

choices.text: Get [missing person] somewhere quiet. They've been away fourteen months.

default.text:
You take them upstairs. Aldous gives you the room at the end of the passage without being asked. He sees the fourteen months in [missing person]'s face and knows at once, rightly, that the last thing they want is questions.

You shut the door. The room is ordinary, and so is the bed. The window looks out on the market square, where the news is beginning to arrive as news arrives in Crestfall, slowly and then all at once.

[missing person] sits down on the bed and looks round the ordinary room.

"It is very loud out there," they say.

"Yes," you say. "You've been somewhere very quiet."

"For fourteen months," they say. And then, quietly, "Thank you for coming."

choices.text: Take charge of the news. Get ahead of the story before the powers in the town shape it.

success.text:
You go quickly round the Tallow and the market. With news like this, the first hour decides everything that comes after.

You give Aldous the version Crestfall needs. You send word to the Rootless camp as fast as it can go. You go to the Compact post and ask to see Vorne himself before Seriva can get to him.

By the time Seriva is back in Crestfall, the account that does Ashenveld most good is already established in three different places. She can change it, but she cannot replace it.

success_at_cost.text: You get ahead of some of it, though not all. Seriva had soldiers who got back before you did, and her version is already going round the Compact post. You manage the rest.

failure.text:
The news moves faster than you do. By the time you have thought what to do about it, Seriva's soldiers have already reported to Vorne, and the story in the Compact post is Seriva's story.

You will have to put it right, which is harder than heading it off.

default: Vorne takes the news as though he had expected it. He had not.
He has you brought to the post. He listens to all you tell him, the ritual and the seal and the mechanism, and Seriva coming and what she did, without once interrupting.
When you have finished he speaks.

default.text:
"Slowed," he says.

"Yes."

He is less ready to talk about withdrawing than he was a minute ago.
default.else:
"The curse will not spread any further," he says.

"No," you say.

default: "We don't know. The seal stops it getting worse. Whether it undoes what's been done, we'll have to watch and see over the next few weeks."

He nods slowly. He is working something out, and you can follow part of it: what this means for his orders, for his task here, for the thirty soldiers and all the stores he has brought to Crestfall, what he is to tell his superiors, and whether the Compact will count this a success or a failure.

default.text: Issa is in the next room. She is worse than she was at the camp, and he knows it.
As you leave he says, "My daughter asked after you."

text.commander:
You know the sum Vorne is doing, because you have done it yourself. He sent thirty soldiers and a senior scholar to secure something of great importance. It has been secured, but by civilians and not by the Compact, and by a method the Compact had no hand in.

In terms of men and money, his task here has been at best half a success. The spread has stopped, but he has not got hold of the mechanism.

"Your daughter," you say. "The seal should slow it in her. Whether it undoes what's been done, we'll see."
text.arcane:
Vorne is thinking about more than his orders. He is thinking about his daughter. The seal has changed things for Issa. The curse is no longer getting worse in her. Whether what has already happened to her will be undone, nobody knows.

He has been trying to put things right for his daughter by having charge of everything round her. Now everything round her has changed, and the question is whether he will change his ways to match.
text.ranger:
Vorne listens, and then asks the question that shows you what he really cares about.

"Issa," he says. "The seal. What does it mean for her?"

You tell him what you know and what you don't. He listens like a father who has been making decisions on too little to go on for weeks, and is making them still.
text.cipher:
What Vorne does next will depend on how he takes this, so you watch him closely.

He isn't angry. He is working it out again. Things are not what they were, and he is a practical man. He will change his position to fit the facts, rather than holding on to the old one.

What you want to know is what the new facts will ask of him, and whether he will accept it.

choices.text: Suggest that the Compact's work here is done, and they can go.

bonus.label: The Compact does not trust you
You and Vorne have an understanding
Issa is still at the camp

success.text:
You put it to him plainly.

The curse is sealed. The Compact said it came to stop the spread, and the spread has been stopped. The mechanism is safe, in that it is no longer dangerous. There is nothing in Crestfall that wants thirty soldiers.

He is quiet a long while.

"My daughter," he says.

"The Rootless camp is the best place for her," you say. "The seal has changed things for her. With time, and the camp's ways, she may get quite better. But she needs to be there, not here, and she chose to be there."

He thinks about it. Then he says, "I shall reduce the garrison. Ten men stay, to keep order while things settle. The rest go within the week."

It is not all you asked for, but it is more than you expected.

success_at_cost.text:
He agrees to fewer soldiers, but he won't go. Thirty become twenty. The checkpoint on the east road stays, and so does the post. He will not leave until Issa is settled one way or the other.

"When she is better, or plainly not going to be," he says, "I shall withdraw altogether."

failure.text:
He won't have it. He is not leaving until he knows all there is to know about the ruins and the mechanism: what it is, what is in it, and what danger it may still be, sealed or not.

"The Compact has a responsibility to this region," he says. "That does not end because one part of the threat has been dealt with."

choices.text: Offer the Compact a full account of the ruins and the mechanism, if they will go.

default.text:
This he looks at differently. A full account of what is in the ruins, what the mechanism is, and the sealing ritual and all it needs would be worth something to the Compact quite apart from soldiering. It is the kind of thing that would make sending him here look worthwhile after all.

"Everything," he says. "The whole of it. The ritual, how the mechanism is made, the language of the old text."

"Yes," you say. [missing person] has fourteen months of notes and Pol has fifteen years of learning. Between them, the account will be complete.

"A fortnight," he says. "I shall withdraw when I have it."

You shake his hand.

default: You take [missing person] to the Rootless camp.
This is a meeting you can't manage, and you don't try to. One of them spent fourteen months in the ruins, and the other sent them there and spent fourteen months wishing she hadn't.

default.text: They saw each other in the ruins and said almost nothing. This is the conversation they did not have.

default: Maret sees them from across the camp and stops where she is. [missing person] sees Maret and stops too. The camp goes on round them, the ordinary business of twenty-three people, and in the middle of it two people with something to say to each other stand quite still.
You leave them to it. Branch turns up at your elbow, not to say anything, only to stand with you while it happens.
text.commander:
You stand with Branch and watch Maret and [missing person] begin the conversation that has waited fourteen months.

"She sent them in," Branch says quietly. "She has never said so to me. But she sent them in."

"I know," you say.

"They are going to be all right," he says. He says it as a man does who has decided how things are going to be, which, with Branch, is generally how they turn out.
text.arcane:
Lira comes and stands beside you while you watch. She is having a good spell, quite herself today, with none of the slowness.

"It's different," she says. "Since this morning. Something's changed."

"Yes," you say.

She thinks about it. "Will I get better?" she asks. She doesn't ask it hopefully. She just wants to know.

"I don't know," you say. "I think you may. I can't promise it." You pause. "But whatever was making you worse has stopped."
text.ranger:
You watch the camp from the edge of it. Lira is more herself today. The plants in the herb garden that answer to the curse have changed, and you read it as a good sign.

So the seal is working, slowly.

Branch says, without looking at you, "You did it." It is as near as he will come to thanking you.
text.cipher:
You watch Maret and [missing person] begin the conversation they needed to have, and you don't listen.

There are some things that are not yours to read.

Branch comes and stands beside you. "Issa asked about you," he says. "She wanted to know who you were."

"What did you tell her?"

"The truth," he says. "That I did not know yet, but I was deciding in your favour." He pauses. "Do not make me change my mind."

choices.text: Go and see Issa, and how the seal has left her.

default.text:
Issa is in the tent that has become hers. She is awake, and more awake than you have ever seen her; the words come to her more quickly today.

"Something's changed," she says when she sees you.

"Yes," you say. "The source of the curse has been sealed. It won't spread any further. And what's already in you..." You pause. "The camp's ways will have less to fight against now."

She looks at her hands. The grey is still at her fingertips. You don't lie to her about whether it will go.

"My father came this morning," she says. "He looked at me and didn't say anything. He just looked."

"Yes," you say. "That sounds like him."

choices.text: Talk to Lira, and find out what the seal feels like from inside.

text: Lira sits with you in the herb garden.

"It's quieter," she says. She doesn't mean the curse. She means the air, the feel of the place. "For three years it's been..." She stops. "Like a noise you get used to. You don't notice it till it changes." She pauses. "It changed this morning. It's quieter. I noticed."
She looks at the plants. "I remembered something today I haven't remembered in two years," she says. "My mother's face. I'd forgotten what she looked like. This morning I remembered."

text.text: By the evening she has lost it again.

text: She doesn't cry. She says it as she says most things, as a plain fact, something she is holding carefully because holding it matters.

success_at_cost.text: Lira is having an uneven day, more herself than yesterday but not altogether. She can tell you something has changed, but not quite what. It is going the right way. You leave her to her work.

failure.text: It is a bad day for Lira. Whatever has changed in the air, it hasn't reached her in any way she can put into words. She goes back to her rope, and you leave her to it.

default.text:
Maret takes out the list. It has gone soft with folding.

"I have not been to the tree line since the seal," she says. "There is nothing to pay. I thought something might come back." She looks at the first line. "Nothing has."

She reads it to you all the same. "My daughter's voice." Then she folds the paper and puts it away.
